opus exports 50 functions. The yaml dictionaries are the deliverable; these are the tooling around them.

## The specification

The dictionary as data. Downstream code should reach the yaml through these rather than parsing it, so there is one place where the shape of the specification is known.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_field_spec()` | Build a combined old-name / new-name / type spec from opus's own shipped YAMLs |
| `op_field_name_map()` | Build field name mapping from data-dict YAML |
| `op_legacy_field_name()` | Extract legacy field name from column details |

## Reading the published archive

The published archive is four parquet files that describe themselves. These are the way in: resolve the root, query a table lazily, or take the whole thing as SQL. Every call is a range request rather than a download, and there is no sidecar catalog to keep in step with the data.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_archive()` | Resolve the archive root |
| `op_con()` | Connect to one raw exchange table |
| `op_catalog()` | Build the SQL catalog from the files' own footers |
| `op_define()` | Apply a named filter definition |
| `op_rename()` | Rename between the legacy and current naming schemes |

## The metadata each file carries

Each file's footer holds its own dictionary, legacy-name crosswalk, enum labels, sentinel policy, coverage and known issues. All of it is read from the same file as the data, so it cannot describe a different vintage of the archive than the one you loaded.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_keys()` | List the metadata keys a file carries |
| `op_dict()` | The data dictionary, one row per column |
| `op_crosswalk()` | The legacy/current name crosswalk, read from the file itself |
| `op_enums()` | Enum code/label pairs |
| `op_definitions()` | Reusable definitions and their translations |
| `op_relationships()` | Resolved join keys and column conflicts |
| `op_coverage()` | What the archive actually covers |
| `op_surveys()` | The survey list, without a live ICES call |
| `op_sentinel_meta()` | The sentinel policy actually applied to this file |
| `op_provenance()` | Who built this file, from what |
| `op_known_issues()` | Known issues affecting this table |

## Converting DATRAS XML to parquet

The four steps of the conversion, in the order they must run: physical types, then names, then sentinels, then the semantic types the wire cannot express. A consumer calling these on its own live fetch gets a result identical to the published archive rather than a near-miss.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_cast_wsdl_types()` | Cast a parsed DATRAS table to its WSDL-declared physical types |
| `op_rename_to_new()` | Rename a DATRAS table from ICES's legacy names to opus's current names |
| `op_strip_sentinels()` | Replace sentinels with NA, where they mean absence |
| `op_cast_to_spec()` | Realise the semantic types the wire format cannot express |
| `op_wsdl_type_overrides()` | The documented WSDL type overrides |

## Sentinels

DATRAS overloads `-9`: in most fields it means "not recorded", in a few it is a documented answer. These read the registry, resolve it to a per-column verdict, and measure the result against real data.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_sentinels()` | Read the sentinel registry |
| `op_sentinel_policy()` | Resolve, per column, whether a sentinel means absence |
| `op_sentinel_audit()` | Count sentinel values per column in a parquet file |

## Field names

ICES is renaming DATRAS fields one table at a time. These separate what ICES *claims* about renames from what survives checking against what the service actually returns.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_datras_field_metadata()` | Fetch ICES's getDatrasFieldList metadata, as ICES publishes it |
| `op_datras_field_list()` | Derive verified Tier 1 legacy field-name mappings, without icesDatras |
| `op_datras_rename_crosswalk()` | Build a rename-ready legacy -> new name crosswalk for one or more tables |

## Reading the DATRAS web service

Primary-source readers. Everything that needs to know what ICES really sends goes through these rather than parsing the service again.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_datras_operations()` | List the DATRAS web service's currently exposed operations |
| `op_datras_operation_types()` | Fetch the field names and types a DATRAS operation actually returns |

## Validation

Is the dictionary well-formed, and does it still describe the data? These matter more than usual under hand-maintenance -- they are what makes editing a large yaml by hand safe.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_validate_spec()` | Validate opus specs against real DATRAS data |
| `op_validate_meta()` | Validate dataset metadata against dictionary |
| `op_validate_data()` | Validate dataset values against dictionary constraints |
| `op_validate_full()` | Run full validation suite |
| `op_validation_problems()` | Flatten a data-dict validation report's problems into a data frame |
| `op_flag_violations()` | Flag rows with violations against dictionary constraints |

## ICES vocabularies

Code semantics from icesVocab. Keys are tied to each field's *legacy* name, which is not obvious until it produces a wrong answer.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_vocab_resolve_datras_key()` | Resolve a DATRAS Tier 1 field to its correct icesVocab key (opus's audited proposal) |
| `op_vocab_resolve_key()` | Resolve a Field Name to Candidate Vocabulary Keys |
| `op_vocab_resolve_guid()` | Resolve an ICES Vocabulary GUID to Its Key -- an Exact Match, Not a Guess |
| `op_vocab_get_types()` | Get ICES Vocabulary Types with Prefix Metadata |
| `op_vocab_get_codes()` | Fetch Code:Meaning Pairs from an ICES Vocabulary Key |
| `op_vocab_first_usable()` | Find the First Vocabulary Key with Usable Codes |

## Parquet and export

Inspecting real data, and rendering the dictionary for other tools.

| Function | |
|---|---|
| `op_inspect_parquet()` | Inspect parquet file schema |
| `op_describe_parquet()` | Describe columns of a parquet file |
| `op_draft_from_parquet()` | Draft a data-dict.yaml from parquet files |
| `op_export_spec()` | Export dictionary as fully-resolved JSON |
| `op_export_data()` | Export dictionary with per-column data profiles |
| `op_render_spec()` | Render a data dictionary as a self-contained HTML page |
